10.1002_anie.202517806: In recent years, oxychloride‐based materials have emerged as a promising solid‐state electrolyte (SSE) candidate owing to its ultrahigh ionic conductivity and decent cathode compatibility. Although the fabrication of SSE coatings for cathode materials has been recognized as a promising strategy, a precise synthesis of oxychloride‐based SSE coating is still not realized due to the lack of appropriate preparation method. As a proof of concept, we propose a superior lithium‐ion conductive aluminum‐based oxychloride (LAOC) coating synthesized by atomic level fabrication strategy with unique self‐limiting reaction mechanism. The LAOC modified lithium cobalt oxide (LCO) cathode exhibits a high capacity retention of 86.4% after 500 cycles at 5 C and significantly improved high‐voltage cycling stability. The outstanding performance is ascribed to the high interfacial ionic conductivity and construction of robust cathode electrolyte interphase. The ionic conductivity of LCO increased from 1.785 × 10 −7 to 2.823 × 10 −6 S cm −1 after LAOC coating. Scanning transmission X‐ray microscopy and transmission electron microscopy reveal that the LAOC coating suppresses interfacial degradation and mitigates the structural collapse of LCO. This study offers great opportunity for the atomic level fabrication of superior ionic conductive oxychloride thin films to realize high performance lithium‐ion batteries.
10.1002_anie.202518058: Copper (Cu) oxides hold great potential for electrochemical synthesis of multi‐carbon (C 2+ ) products from CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR), but a clear picture correlating chemical bond characteristics in pristine Cu oxides with inevitable reconstruction during CO 2 RR remains underexplored. Herein, we report our findings in the regulation of Cu─O bond polarizability in layered cuprates (Ln 2 CuO 4 , Ln = La, Pr, Nd, Sm, and Gd) by an A‐site rare‐earth modulation strategy, to promote surface reconstruction toward high‐efficiency C 2+ electrosynthesis. In particular, the optimized Pr 2 CuO 4 bulk material with largest bond polarizability exhibits the best performance, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of ∼80% for C 2+ products and a C 2+ partial current density of 376.2 mA cm −2 at −1.7 V versus RHE as well as maintaining robust durability at 200 mA cm −2 in a membrane electrode assembly. Experimental and theoretical results reveal that larger Cu─O bond polarizability, characterized as increased bond length and decreased valence state, accelerates the Cu‐O bond breaking that can lead to the formation of ultrasmall, highly dispersed, and strained Cu nanoparticles. These reconstructed metallic Cu particles, together with Cu/Pr 2 CuO 4 interface, function as dual active sites to improve * CO coverage and lower the energy barrier for C─C coupling, resulting in the enhanced C 2+ selectivity.
10.1016_j.seta.2026.105514: Industrial alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) is commercially mature, but inconsistent reporting limits comparisons of stack designs. This review connects public specifications for 29 products from 26 original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) with scientific, component and patent evidence through July 2026. A documented 110-candidate screening applies technology, commercial-offering and individual-stack-size criteria, followed by an energy-consumption/deployment evidence check. The commercial evidence supports two development routes: single-element/modular-cell designs more consistently emphasise high current density, whereas integrated, predominantly cylindrical stacks generally disclose lower numerical ranges. This is a tendency in the reviewed products, not an intrinsic geometrical or pressure limit. Numerical current–density evidence is available for nine records, including explicitly qualified family and shared-platform statements; other sources provide qualitative evidence. Different operating conditions and energy boundaries prevent a controlled performance ranking. The 455-publication patent inventory identifies developments coupling catalytic activity with coating adhesion, separator pore architecture, electrode contact, flow and thermal management, and variable-load operation. Patent disclosure does not demonstrate implementation in a commercial product. Linking these mechanisms to the commercial evidence defines testable development priorities and a minimum reporting dataset. The industrial objective is higher current density sustained at comparable energy consumption, pressure, purity and lifetime.
10.1109_tie.2026.3672770: Traditional integrated voltage equalization circuits with compact size and low cost. However, each secondary winding can only balance individual cells, and although capable of charge/discharge balancing, cannot achieve autonomous self-balancing functionality. To overcome their shortcomings, an integrated balancing topology based on a CLLLC resonant converter is proposed in this article. First, each secondary winding attains dual-cell balancing capability by incorporating a voltage doubler circuit that capitalizes on the symmetrical voltage ripple characteristics inherent to full-bridge CLLLC resonant converters. This innovative configuration effectively doubles the voltage equalization capacity while maintaining identical transformer winding quantities. Second, the zero-voltage switching (ZVS) across all MOSFETs throughout charge and discharge cycles through meticulous topological optimization of the CLLLC converter topology is guaranteed based on the operational mechanism of the integrated balancer. This inherent soft-switching characteristic enables the system to maintain autonomous self-balancing functionality even under idle operating conditions. Experimental validation was conducted to demontrate that the transferred energy is effectively balanced during charging, discharging, and idle conditions by the proposed integrated balancing circuit on a system with six supercapacitors. Peak efficiencies of 92.47% (18.96 W), 92.97% (12.34 W), and 92.67% (9.87 W) are demonstrated in the charge, discharge, and self-balance modes, respectively.
